title: Barts — Audit

cro.summary: The largest conversion blocker on the BARTS webshop is the absence of trust signals: new visitors see no reviews, stars, or customer ratings on the homepage, while this is crucial for a first purchase. In addition, the homepage lacks a clear value proposition — the primary CTA texts are logistical ('Returns within 30 days', 'Free shipping') rather than inspiring or distinctive. At annual revenue of around €7 million, even a small conversion-rate improvement can quickly yield tens of thousands of extra euros.
topActions: Add review stars and an average rating on the homepage, immediately visible without scrolling — connect this to a review platform such as Trustpilot or Kiyoh so new visitors immediately see that others are satisfied.

Rewrite the homepage headline into a concrete value proposition that in one sentence tells what sets BARTS apart (for example: brand promise, collection breadth, or quality), instead of putting only shipping and return terms at the top.
Add product information to your product listings in Google so stars and ratings appear next to your search results — this increases clicks from Google without extra ad spend.

phases.name: Close the leaks
actions: Activate a content delivery network (a layer that stores your pages and images closer to the visitor) for your Magento installation — Cloudflare or Fastly are proven options that run within a day and immediately improve load time on mobile and desktop
Compress the hero image at the top of every page and set the load order so visible page content is shown first — goal: mobile load time under 2.5 seconds

Set up server-side conversion measurement for Meta (Facebook/Instagram) and Google Ads: purchases are then sent directly from your server to the ad platform instead of via the customer's browser, so clickers who refuse cookies are counted too
Activate a cookie-consent solution that complies with GDPR and works with server-side conversion measurement — this is the legal and measurement foundation for everything that follows

Set up domain security for email: activate SPF (a list of servers allowed to send mail on behalf of Barts), DKIM (a digital signature per email), and DMARC (a policy that blocks fake emails) — work with your email provider, executable in less than a working day
phases.objective: Stop the direct revenue loss by closing the three largest leaks: mobile load time that is too slow, disappearing ad conversions, and email that lands in spam.
phases.expectedOutcome: Mobile load time under 2.5 seconds, attribution loss drops from 35% to under 10%, email campaigns land structurally better in the inbox, cookie strategy complies with GDPR

phases.name: Increase conversion and visibility
actions: Add structured product data to your product pages (technical information that tells Google what you sell, including price and availability) so your products qualify for Google Shopping and your search results stand out with extra product details

Connect your review platform (Trustpilot, Kiyoh, or similar) to your product pages so stars and ratings become visible next to your search results in Google — this immediately increases clicks on organic results
Add customer reviews and an average review score on the homepage, visible without scrolling — new visitors immediately see that others are satisfied, which raises conversion of unknown visitors
Rewrite the homepage headline into a concrete brand promise that in one sentence tells why customers buy from Barts, instead of putting only logistical promises (free shipping, returns) at the top
Run a targeted analysis on the busiest product pages and collection pages to identify and fix the one demonstrated conversion blocker — use the restored measurement data from Phase 1 as the basis
Configure the Sizebay scripts (size-advice tool) so they load later and do not delay visible page content — technically: load them asynchronously after the first visible part of the page
phases.objective: Turn the recovered load speed and correct measurement data into measurably more orders via better visibility in Google, stronger trust signals on the site, and higher conversion on busy pages.
dependencies: Phase 1 complete: server-side measurement active and load time under 2.5s — without correct measurement data, CRO decisions in Phase 2 are unreliable
phases.expectedOutcome: Product pages appear with stars in Google search results, organic click-through rate rises, conversion on homepage and product pages increases measurably, bounce on paid traffic drops further

phases.name: Prepare platform choice and scale
actions: Inventory all Magento 2 integrations Barts actively uses (including Sizebay and Storyblok) and map migration costs and risks for Shopify Plus — do this now that Phases 1 and 2 have produced concrete performance figures against which you can set the business case

Build email automation for at least three flows that are now likely missing or unmeasured: welcome email for new subscribers, recovery email for abandoned carts, and a win-back email for customers who have not ordered in a while — at an industry average of 30% email revenue, this is the largest unused channel
Optimise newsletter signup on the site: the signup module sits in the footer but is not prominent enough — test a more visible placement or a popup with a concrete reason to subscribe

Add product data for Google Merchant Center so products also appear in Google Shopping ads and free Shopping results — this was marked as not-ready and is now feasible now that product data from Phase 2 is present

Make a decision on platform migration based on the inventory: continue on Magento 2 with structural performance investments, or start a phased migration to Shopify Plus — at €7 million annual revenue the business case for Shopify Plus is real but requires careful safeguarding of existing integrations
phases.objective: Based on concrete performance figures from Phases 1 and 2, make a well-founded decision on whether Magento 2 will be replaced by Shopify Plus over time, and in the meantime build out email channels as a structural revenue layer.
dependencies: Phase 1 complete: domain security active so email flows actually arrive
Phase 2 complete: product data and review connection present as a basis for Google Merchant Center
phases.expectedOutcome: Email channel generates measurable revenue via automated flows, Google Shopping active, platform choice for the next three years locked in with a concrete migration plan or investment plan for Magento 2

quickWins: Compress the largest image at the top of every landing page and set it to load first — executable in one day, immediately lowers mobile load time toward the 2.5s threshold and reduces drop-off of paid clickers
Set SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for your domain via DNS management — less than half a working day for a developer, prevents newsletters from landing in spam, and protects your brand name against abuse
topPriorities: Cut mobile load time from 2.7s to under 2.5s by activating a content delivery network and loading the largest image at the top of the page first — this is the direct cause of 35% burned ad budget

Turn on domain security for email (SPF, DKIM, and DMARC): without this, newsletters structurally land in spam and scammers can send mail in Barts' name — at an industry average of 30% email revenue this is €170,000+/mo of risk
Add server-side conversion measurement for Meta and Google Ads so 35% of purchases that are currently invisible are counted — algorithms learn on complete data and buy cheaper clicks
Add product data and review stars to your search results in Google (via technical product data on your pages) — this increases clicks from organic search without extra ad spend
Activate a cookie-consent solution that complies with GDPR and works with your ad platforms — currently completely missing, a legal risk and a data-quality risk
roadmap.northStarMetric: Mobile conversion rate (currently unmeasured — set as a goal: at least at the desktop benchmark of 2.0%)
roadmap.executiveSummary: Barts loses up to €70,700 in demonstrable revenue each month because the mobile store loads just too slowly, ad clicks evaporate before the page is ready, and email campaigns structurally land in spam more often because basic domain security is missing. The path forward is clear: first close the leaking funnel (speed, email security, tracking), then expand visibility in Google, and after that carefully prepare the platform choice for the next growth phase.

deliverability.summary: This domain's email infrastructure has three critical gaps: no sender verification is set up, so newsletters structurally land in spam more often, and scammers can impersonate this brand without mail providers being able to block them. At revenue of ~€583k per month — where email in the industry generates 30% of revenue on average — this webshop potentially misses €170k+ per month through poor inbox placement. This is the highest-priority technical fix in the entire audit.
topActions: Set a sender lock for your domain (SPF): this tells mail providers such as Gmail and Outlook which servers are authorised to send email on behalf of your brand — without this, your emails are labelled as suspicious and land in spam more often.

Activate a digital signature for your outgoing emails (DKIM): every newsletter or order confirmation then gets an encrypted authenticity stamp proving the mail really comes from you — this immediately improves inbox placement at Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo.

Put a domain protection policy (DMARC) in place at least at 'quarantine': this prevents criminals from sending fake emails in your store's name, and signals to major mail providers that your domain is trustworthy — which structurally improves your newsletter open rates.

adBounceRevenue.summary: Of every 1,000 people who click an ad, 28 extra drop off versus the normal baseline — almost entirely because the page loads just too slowly on mobile (load time sits 0.2 seconds above the critical threshold). At the same time, about a third of all purchases never reach your ad platforms: your algorithms therefore learn on incomplete data and keep buying structurally too-expensive clicks. At monthly revenue of around €583,000 and an ad budget that is substantial at this volume, that is a concrete and avoidable cost.
topActions: Cut landing-page load time on mobile by at least 0.3 seconds (from 2.7s to under 2.5s): this is the direct cause of the extra drop-offs after an ad click. Practically: compress the largest image at the top of the page and make sure it loads first. This is executable within one sprint and immediately lowers drop-off.

Fix the missing tracking pixels: currently your measurement setup does not register a substantial share of purchases. As a result, Meta and Google steer their ad budget on roughly two thirds of actual conversions — which leads to higher cost per click and lower return on your ad investment. Add server-side passthrough (a technical layer where purchases are sent directly from your server to the ad platform, instead of only via the customer's browser), so purchases from people who refuse cookies are counted too.

Activate a consent-management solution that fully works with cookie rules: this layer is currently completely missing. Without it you do not meet GDPR requirements and you miss the ability to still send conversion data back to your ad platforms with privacy-friendly signals. This protects both your legal position and the data quality your algorithms work with.

keyWins: Faster and more reliable payment page via Shopify — proven higher conversion on mobile and desktop
Shopify-native tracking replaces the current loose setup and lowers attribution loss from an estimated 35% to under 15%
Less server maintenance and infrastructure cost: no more self-hosted Magento server, scales automatically with peak traffic
Sizebay and Storyblok are both available within Shopify, so size advice and content management do not need to be replaced
shopifyMigration.summary: Barts.eu runs on Magento 2 — a powerful platform, but expensive to maintain and slow to improve at this scale. The combination of slow mobile load time, a missing cookie strategy, and an estimated 35% attribution loss means revenue is currently left on the table. Migration to Shopify Plus is worth serious consideration, but requires a careful approach because of the integrations Magento 2 typically brings.
keyRisks: At this revenue, Magento 2 often contains custom work in discounts, pricing rules, or B2B specifications — those must be fully mapped before migration starts, otherwise surprises along the way are expensive
No content delivery network and no server-side tracking are already a problem — during migration both must be solved at the same time, otherwise you push the risk forward
shopifyMigration.rationale: Barts.eu has annual revenue of around 7 million euros and runs on a self-hosted Magento 2 environment without a content delivery network (a network that serves your site faster worldwide). Mobile load time sits at 2.7 seconds — just above the threshold where visitors drop off, and without a CDN there is no buffer for peak traffic. The estimated 35% attribution loss — meaning more than a third of every euro of revenue is not correctly attributed to the right marketing channel — shows up monthly in wrong budget decisions. No cookie-consent strategy is active, which is a risk under current privacy regulation. The payment page looks solid: iDEAL, Klarna, Bancontact, and PayPal are present, guest checkout is available, and elapsed time is 5.9 seconds — acceptable but improvable. Sizebay (size-advice tool) and Storyblok (content management) are active and must be safeguarded in a migration. The combination of Magento 2 maintenance cost, the performance gap, and the tracking problem means Shopify Plus has a real business case — but the custom integrations Magento 2 typically has at this revenue first require a thorough inventory.
topActions: Inventory all customisations in the current Magento 2 environment: which discount rules, customer groups, integrations, and automations exist — this determines the real migration complexity

Fix the attribution problem regardless of the platform decision: install a cookie-consent strategy and improve the connection between your ad channels and your analytics — at €583,000 monthly revenue, 35% loss is an urgent problem
Run a business-case calculation: set Magento 2 annual costs (server, developers, licences, updates) against Shopify Plus — in many cases the switch pays for itself within 12 months

techArchitecture.summary: The webshop runs on Magento 2 on its own server without demonstrable use of an external content delivery network, which means every visitor fetches the page from one central server — a fragile and slow starting point at peak traffic. On mobile it takes over 2.7 seconds before the main page content is visible, and on desktop even more than 4 seconds — at revenue of around €583,000 per month, every extra second of wait is a direct hit on conversions. In addition, ad conversions are largely missed because all measurement data only arrives via the visitor's browser, which with modern privacy settings and ad blockers structurally leads to under-measurement.
topActions: Put an external content delivery network (a layer that stores and serves pages and images closer to the visitor) in front of your Magento installation. This immediately and noticeably lowers load time on mobile and desktop, distributes traffic so your server is not overloaded during campaigns or peaks, and eliminates the current risk that one server outage takes your entire store down.

Improve mobile load speed from 2.7 seconds to under 2.5 seconds by enabling page caching at server level and configuring Magento so returning visitors get a stored version of the page instead of the server rebuilding everything each time. At your current revenue scale, every half-second of speed gain yields an estimated tens of thousands of euros in extra monthly revenue.

Set up server-side conversion measurement for Meta (Facebook/Instagram) and Google Ads: you then send measurement data directly from your server to the ad platforms, instead of relying on the visitor's browser. Ad blockers and privacy settings currently intercept a significant share of your conversion signals, so your campaigns are less well optimised than they could be — at a monthly ad budget at your scale, this concretely means you pay for reach whose results stay invisible.

coreThesis: Barts loses visitors each month before they can buy anything, because the mobile page loads too slowly and some orders do not arrive properly in the ad platforms.

layers.name: The Door

metrics.metric: How quickly do visitors see your products?
metrics.signal: Visitors wait 2.7s before they see your products — too slow, they drop off
metrics.whatWeMeasure: How long visitors wait before they see anything at all — every extra second of waiting costs customers
metrics.calculationNote: Slow load time → visitors drop off → revenue you miss

metrics.metric: Does the page respond immediately to clicks?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: Whether clicks on buttons and menus work immediately or visitors have to wait
metrics.calculationNote: Slow response → visitors think it is broken → they leave

metrics.metric: How many visitors leave before they see anything?
metrics.signal: 48% leave immediately — 3% above healthy, that is lost revenue
metrics.whatWeMeasure: The share of your visitors who click away immediately because the page loads too slowly
metrics.calculationNote: Extra leavers × average order value × chance of purchase = missed revenue

metrics.metric: How much ad money evaporates before the page loads?
metrics.signal: 35% of your ad budget burns — the clicker never really sees your store
metrics.whatWeMeasure: The share of your ad budget you pay for but get no customer back — the clicker is gone before the page is ready
metrics.calculationNote: Evaporated share × monthly ad budget = directly burned money

layers.name: The Engine

metrics.metric: How many apps slow your store down?
metrics.signal: 4 apps active — within a healthy range
metrics.whatWeMeasure: Whether the Shopify apps you pay for cost your store more in revenue than they deliver
metrics.calculationNote: Extra apps above a healthy range → slower → fewer sales → revenue loss

metrics.metric: How much surplus code is your store dragging along?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: How much unnecessary code your theme loads that adds nothing but still costs load time
metrics.calculationNote: Surplus weight → longer load time → fewer orders → revenue gone

metrics.metric: How many external scripts block your store?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: External services (tracking, chat, reviews) that make the store wait before they are ready
metrics.calculationNote: Extra wait from external services → visitors drop off → less revenue

metrics.metric: How quickly does your server respond?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: How long Shopify itself needs before anything comes back at all — often a hosting/plan problem
metrics.calculationNote: Slow server → slow entire store → fewer orders → less revenue

goodSignals: 4 apps active — within a healthy range
layers.coreQuestion: What makes your stack slow, and what does that cost?

layers.name: The Leak

metrics.metric: Does the payment page leak customers?
metrics.signal: no obstacles found on the payment page
metrics.whatWeMeasure: Friction between 'add to cart' and 'thanks for your order' — the most expensive place to lose customers
metrics.calculationNote: Every obstacle on the payment page costs customers who already wanted to buy — direct revenue loss

metrics.metric: Does the page jump away under the cursor?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: Buttons or images that shift while visitors try to click — feels untrustworthy
metrics.calculationNote: Shifting elements → misclicks and frustration → visitors give up → less revenue

metrics.metric: Verliest mobiel veel meer dan desktop?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: The gap between your mobile and desktop store — 70% of your visitors are mobile, so every percent of difference counts twice
metrics.calculationNote: Large mobile/desktop gap → most visitors on the worst-performing version → large revenue loss

metrics.metric: Which pages leak the most revenue?
metrics.signal: 1 thing on your most important pages that stops visitors from ordering
metrics.whatWeMeasure: Product pages, collection pages, and cart pages with demonstrable conversion blockers
metrics.calculationNote: Conversion blockers on your busiest pages → direct revenue left on the table

keySignals: 1 thing on your most important pages that stops visitors from ordering
goodSignals: no obstacles found on the payment page
layers.coreQuestion: Where does conversion leak through technical friction?
improvementSignals: 1 thing on your most important pages that stops visitors from ordering

layers.name: Efficiency

metrics.metric: How many more visitors would buy with a fast store?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: What % of your visitors buy now vs how many would buy if your store were as fast as the competition
metrics.calculationNote: Difference in purchase likelihood between your store and a fast store → direct growth opportunity

metrics.metric: How much revenue are you leaving on the table each month?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: The gap between what you earn now and what you would earn with the same visitors but a fast store
metrics.calculationNote: ~32,623 visitors × difference in purchase likelihood × €120 average order

metrics.metric: How much cheaper does each new customer become?
metrics.signal: Acquisition cost already optimal at current performance
metrics.whatWeMeasure: What it currently costs you to acquire a new customer vs what that would be if the store did not leak
metrics.calculationNote: Fewer leavers → more purchases per euro of ad budget → lower acquisition cost per customer

metrics.metric: How much more do you get from the same ad budget?
metrics.whatWeMeasure: How much extra revenue your ad budget yields once visitors who make it in actually convert
metrics.calculationNote: More visitors who buy at the same ad spend → directly higher revenue per ad euro

layers.coreQuestion: How much more revenue is sitting in existing traffic?

ceoTriggers.kpi: ROAS drops while ad spend rises
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: The store leaks visitors before they convert. More traffic into a leaking funnel makes the problem worse.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Every extra euro in ads returns less. More budget ≠ more revenue.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You are pouring water into a bucket with holes. We close the holes so every euro of ad spend returns more.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Mobile converts dramatically lower than desktop
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: The mobile–desktop gap is almost never a UX problem. It is a performance problem: mobile is more sensitive to load time.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Desktop converts 2–3x better than mobile, while 70%+ of traffic is mobile.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: 70% of your visitors are mobile. If that half converts this poorly, you are leaving the most money where the most traffic sits.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: If your funnel leaks, you need more clicks per conversion — and every click costs money.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: It costs more and more to acquire a new customer. Marketing is getting more expensive.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Your CPA is not rising only because ads are getting more expensive. Fix the store and your CPA drops — without changing your ad strategy.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Market share declining against comparable product
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: With comparable products, the store with the best buying experience wins. Speed becomes the differentiator.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Competitors with a comparable product are growing faster.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Your product is not the problem. Your store experience is the problem. The customer goes to the store where it is easier and faster.

ceoTriggers.kpi: No organic growth despite SEO investment
ceoTriggers.alarmSignal: No ranking growth after 6 months of SEO
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Google rewards Core Web Vitals in ranking. A slow site loses to a fast competitor.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: SEO efforts are not paying off. Rankings stagnate or decline.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Google does not rank on content alone. They rank on experience. Your Core Web Vitals are a ranking factor — and right now they are working against you.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: AI agents rely on structured data and API accessibility. Without that, you are invisible.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Customers ask ChatGPT/Gemini for product advice and your brand does not appear.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: In 2 years, 30%+ of product searches will start with an AI agent. If that agent cannot find you, you do not exist in that world.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Shopify app costs rise but results don't
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Every app adds weight to the store. You pay twice: the subscription + the conversion loss the app causes.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Every month more apps, more subscriptions, but no measurable effect on revenue.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You pay monthly for apps that slow your store down. Some cost more in conversion loss than they deliver in functionality.
ceoTriggers.tradualSolution: Revenue Leak Audit™ — Layer 2: The Engine

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Checkout latency and layout shifts break trust at the critical moment.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: 3 out of 4 customers who add something to their cart do not check out.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You already convinced the customer — they clicked 'add'. And then you lose them in checkout. That is the most expensive loss there is.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: More visitors do not capture more revenue because the funnel keeps leaking in proportion — it is a conversion problem, not an acquisition problem. Extra traffic into a leaking funnel makes the damage larger.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Visitor numbers are rising, but revenue is not growing with them. More traffic ≠ more sales.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You are growing in visitors but not in revenue. That means: the store itself is the bottleneck, not your marketing. Close the leaks and every extra visitor finally yields revenue.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: A declining average order value with an unchanged assortment points to cross-sell and upsell that are not working — or a product page that only sends visitors to the cheapest item.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Customers are buying less per order, while the assortment has not gotten smaller.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You leave revenue on the table with every order. A customer who is already buying is the easiest customer to sell something extra to — but the store does nothing with that.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: A low page score combined with a large speed gap between mobile and desktop structurally pushes conversion rate below the industry average. Funnel friction eats conversion.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Of every 100 visitors, fewer than 2 buy. Competitors get more from the same traffic.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Every visitor who does not buy is lost acquisition cost. At a conversion rate under 2%, you leave revenue on the table every day that your competitors do capture.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: More than half of paid clickers leave the page before it is fully loaded — directly burned ad budget with no chance of a sale.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: More than half of the people who click an ad leave immediately without doing anything.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You pay for every click, but more than half of those clickers never really see your store. The page is too slow — and the ad euro is then gone immediately.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Customer value barely covers acquisition cost
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: With rising acquisition costs and a leaking funnel, customer value falls relative to acquisition cost. The unit economics break — each customer costs relatively more and more.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: It costs more and more to acquire a customer, but that customer does not buy enough back to justify it.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: A healthy e-commerce business earns back at least three times the acquisition cost per customer. If that ratio falls, it can no longer be the market alone — then the store itself is leaking.

revenueLeak.methodologyNote: Measured estimate. Revenue: €583,333/mo (provided by operator). Measured via SE Ranking: 32,609 organic + 14 paid sessions/mo (32,623 total). CVR 14.90% derived from measured traffic. €120 AOV, €87,500/mo ad spend. Based on publicly measurable signals. Use as an indication, not as a definitive audit outcome.

auditSummary: Automated outside-only scan of Magento 2 store (https://www.barts.eu/nl/). 5 technical risks and 2 opportunities identified.

adTrafficImpact.methodologyNote: Measured estimate based on Google CrUX correlations (LCP/INP → bounce rate). Measured via SE Ranking: 14 paid sessions/mo. 2% CVR, €120 AOV. Use as an indication, not as a measured benchmark.

biggestTechRisk: 35% of your ad budget burns because visitors drop off before the page is visible — paid clicks that never yield anything.

bloatWhatMustGo.reason: Your Magento store delivers all pages and files directly from one server, without a stop via a CDN (a network that places your content closer to your visitors). This means every visitor — including those in other countries — waits on that one server. At €7 million annual revenue this is the highest-yielding technical improvement: a CDN such as Cloudflare costs €20–200 per month and can improve load time by 200–800ms, which at your revenue scale amounts to a multiple of recovered conversion loss.

These are two scripts from the same size-advice tool (Sizebay) that together delay your page load. Both load early while they are only needed when a customer on a product page asks for size advice. By starting them later, the delay they currently cause disappears without losing the functionality.

Storyblok is an external content platform. How heavy this script is was not measured, but if it loads on every page while it is only needed for editors or specific content blocks, it costs unnecessary load time. Potentially replaceable or restrictable once you have a CDN and more visibility into what this script actually does on product pages.

croObservations.estImpact: Medium — every 100ms above 2.5s correlates with ~1% conversion loss.
croObservations.observation: Mobile LCP is 2.7s — above Google's 2.5s 'good' threshold.

croObservations.estImpact: High — trust signals on the homepage demonstrably reduce bounce rate for new visitors. Missing social proof raises the barrier for a first purchase.
croObservations.observation: No reviews, stars, or trust signals detected on the homepage. No review-platform widget (Trustpilot, Kiyoh, etc.), no AggregateRating schema, and no rating pattern in page text.

croObservations.estImpact: Trust signals on the homepage demonstrably lower bounce for new visitors. At monthly revenue of ~€583k, a 1–2% improvement in click-through from homepage to product page can already yield €6,000–€12,000 extra per month.
croObservations.observation: No reviews, stars, or customer ratings are visible on the homepage. For a new visitor who does not yet know BARTS, that means the most important signal that others are already satisfied customers is missing. This raises the barrier to click through or make a first purchase.

croObservations.estImpact: A clear, distinctive headline raises relevance for new visitors and lowers bounce rate. Industry studies show that improving the above-the-fold value proposition typically yields 2–5% more click-through to product pages.
croObservations.observation: The texts at the top of the page — 'Returns within 30 days' and 'Free shipping from €50' — are service benefits, not a value proposition. A visitor seeing the site for the first time does not understand in five seconds why they should be at BARTS rather than a competitor. There is no H1 heading on the homepage.

croObservations.estImpact: Every 100 milliseconds of load-speed improvement correlates with about 1% more conversion on mobile. Bringing it under 2.5 seconds is estimated to yield 0.5–1% more conversions among mobile visitors.
croObservations.observation: Mobile load speed sits just above the threshold Google considers 'good': the page is fully visible after almost 2.7 seconds, while 2.5 seconds is the standard. Every extra tenth of a second costs measurable mobile visitors who drop off before they see anything.

croObservations.estImpact: Stars in search results raise click-through rate by 10–15% on average without extra ad budget. For a site with €7 million annual revenue and organic traffic as a channel, this can be substantial.
croObservations.observation: Product pages lack the technical markup Google needs to show stars and ratings in search results. That means you miss advertising-equivalent free search traffic: competitors with visible stars in Google attract more clicks at the same position.

croObservations.estImpact: Email marketing delivers around 30% of revenue on average for webshops. A higher signup rate through a concrete offer at signup (e.g. 10% off the first order) can grow the email list faster and structurally raise retention revenue.
croObservations.observation: A newsletter signup is present in the footer. However, there is no visible incentive (such as a welcome discount or exclusive content) to actively prompt visitors to subscribe. Without a clear benefit, the signup rate stays well below potential.
